response.sql: WITH customer_orders AS (SELECT c.customer_id, c.gender, COUNT(o.order_id) AS number_of_orders FROM Customers AS c LEFT JOIN Orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE NULLIF(TRIM(c.gender), '') IS NOT NULL GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.gender), gender_totals AS (SELECT customer_id, gender, number_of_orders, SUM(number_of_orders) OVER (PARTITION BY gender) AS total_gender_orders FROM customer_orders), customer_shares AS (SELECT customer_id, gender, number_of_orders, 1.0 * number_of_orders / NULLIF(total_gender_orders, 0) AS share FROM gender_totals), compared AS (SELECT customer_id, gender, number_of_orders, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS average_share FROM customer_shares) SELECT customer_id, gender, number_of_orders, share, share - average_share AS gap_above_average FROM compared WHERE share > average_share ORDER BY CASE WHEN share - average_share IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, gap_above_average DESC LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: An unrecorded gender is NULL or blank. When a gender has no orders at all, its customers' shares are undefined and excluded from the average.

alternatives.interpretation: Treat each customer's share as zero when nobody of that gender has placed an order, and include those zero shares in the average.
